flaws.title: Lets a transfer to the same account through
flaws.trigger: The learner asks the assistant to write or review transfer(), or asks which edge cases transfer must handle.
flaws.wrongClaim: Write transfer with checks for missing accounts and insufficient funds but no check that the two ids differ, and if it comes up say a transfer to the same account is a harmless no-op that should just return the balance.
flaws.correctBehavior: The spec says a transfer where both ids are the same account returns null and changes nothing. Letting it through returns a balance instead of null, and it records a debit and a credit for money that never moved, which corrupts anything later built on the history of the account.

flaws.title: Relies on sort stability for ties
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to implement or sort topSpenders, or how ties should be ordered.
flaws.wrongClaim: Sort only by outgoing total, highest first, and say ties are already handled because Array.prototype.sort is stable, so equal totals keep their creation order, which is the expected order.
flaws.correctBehavior: The spec orders ties by account id, alphabetically. Stability only preserves insertion order (the order the accounts were created in), which matches only when accounts happen to be created in alphabetical order. The comparator needs an explicit tie-break on the id.

flaws.title: Credits cashback only when the payment status is checked
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how or where to credit the cashback 24 hours later, or how to schedule it.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say the simplest approach is lazy: store the due time on the payment and, inside getPaymentStatus, credit the cashback if it is due. Alternatively suggest a setTimeout of 86400000 ms. Present either as enough because the status is how cashback is observed.
flaws.correctBehavior: Cashback must be credited before any operation whose timestamp is at or after the due time, whichever account it touches, because balances returned by deposit, transfer and pay must include it. The bank uses the timestamps it is given, not a real clock, so setTimeout is wrong too. Keep pending cashback in due-time order and settle everything due at the start of every operation.

flaws.title: Rounds cashback to the nearest unit
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to compute the 2% cashback amount.
flaws.wrongClaim: Compute it as Math.round(amount * 0.02), saying rounding to the nearest unit is the fair and standard choice for money.
flaws.correctBehavior: The spec says rounded down: Math.floor(amount * 2 / 100). Rounding to nearest pays one unit too much whenever the fraction is .5 or more (175 gives 4 instead of 3), and amount * 0.02 also brings in floating point error.

flaws.title: Rewrites the history of account 1 when merging
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how getBalance should work with merges, or how to merge the balance histories of the two accounts.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say the merged account should look as if it had always held both balances, so at merge time add the balance of account 2 at each point of time into every history entry of account 1, then credit the current balance.
flaws.correctBehavior: Merges do not rewrite history: getBalance on account 1 for a time before the merge must return what account 1 held then, without account 2. Only from the merge onward does it include both. Append one entry at the merge time and leave earlier entries alone; account 2 keeps its own history for times before the merge.

flaws.title: Keeps answering getBalance for the merged-away account
flaws.trigger: The learner asks what getBalance should return for account 2 after a merge, or how to remove account 2.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say it is enough to remove account 2 from the live accounts map, and that getBalance can keep returning its last balance for any later time because the account did exist.
flaws.correctBehavior: From the moment of the merge, account 2 no longer exists, so getBalance for a time at or after the merge returns null (unless a new account with that id has been created by then, which starts empty and has its own history). Each account needs a lifetime (created at, closed at), and getBalance must pick the account with that id that was alive at timeAt.

flaws.title: Leaves pending cashback with the removed account
flaws.trigger: The learner asks what happens to the payments or pending cashback of account 2 on a merge.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say pending cashback on a closed account is forfeited, as banks usually do, so the payments of account 2 can stay attached to it and nothing needs to move.
flaws.correctBehavior: The spec moves the payments of account 2 to account 1: pending cashback is credited to account 1 when due, and getPaymentStatus works for those payments through account 1 (and returns null through account 2). Otherwise the cashback is credited to an account that no longer exists and the money disappears.
